messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: GPU-MEM-PRESSURE on pool=infer-gpu-7 nodes=[g-7-15,g-7-18] metric=nv_gpu_mem_used_pct threshold=88% -> PagerDuty PD12345 fired
pagerduty-bot: PD12345: page sent to sam (oncall). Escalation policy: gpu-memory. Link: https://pagerduty.example/PD12345
sam (oncall): acked — I'm on it. pinging infra.
leo (infra): looking now, grabbing nvidia-smi from g-7-15
sam (oncall): paste of nvidia-smi output:
```
Fri Mar 13 09:10:12 2026
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        | Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
|  0  A100-40GB        Off      | 00000000:3B:00.0 | Off    | N/A                  |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Processes:                                                                  |
|  GPU   GI   CI        PID   Type   Process name                  GPU Memory |
|        ID   ID                                     Usage               |
|    0   N/A  N/A     24123    C   python /opt/redwood/runtime/main.py   38972MiB |
|    0   N/A  N/A     24187    C   python /opt/redwood/runtime/worker.py    37940MiB |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
sam (oncall): logs show repeated errors in runtime logs: `CUDA error: out of memory` and then `failed to allocate KV cache shard`
```
[09:11:02] runtime ERROR: allocate_kv_cache failed: CUDA out of memory (2)
[09:11:03] runtime WARN: falling back to smaller kv-shard but allocation still fails
[09:11:05] kernel: NVRM: GPU 00000000:3B:00.0: Xid (PCI:0000:3B:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
```
leo (infra): kv-cache eviction metric is weird — eviction_count ~0 while kv-cache size monotonically grows. sending metric query: `sum(redis_kvcache_evictions{pool="infer-gpu-7"}) by (instance)` — result 0.
leo (infra): hypothesis: a regression in kvcache eviction policy after the last runtime rollout (v3.12.0) caused unbounded growth and eventual GPU OOM on high-concurrency shards.
sam (oncall): immediate mitigation: reduce concurrency on pool, enable fallback routing to cpu-fallback for critical customers, restart offender pods on nodes g-7-15 and g-7-18 to free GPU mem.
sam (oncall): commands I ran:
```
# scale down concurrency for pool
rictl pool update infer-gpu-7 --concurrency=1
# route 30% of traffic for tier=critical to cpu-fallback
rictl route modify --from-pool infer-gpu-7 --to-pool cpu-fallback --selector "tier=critical" --percent 30
# restart runtime on nodes
skopeo exec --host g-7-15 -- systemctl restart redwood-runtime
kubectl delete pod runtime-24123 -n redwood-inference --grace-period=10 --force
```
nina (sre): support note: we've opened an incident ticket SRE-4392 and messaged support@customers. Early impact: three hosted customers (cust-a, cust-b, cust-c) saw elevated 5xx rates and latency > 2s between 09:09-09:22 UTC. No enterprise SLA breach yet but we're tracking.
sam (oncall): mitigation in progress — after restart memory usage on g-7-15 dropped, one process reclaimed memory, nv_gpu_mem_used_pct went from 92% -> 48% on that node. Observability shows kvcache purge triggered after restart.
leo (infra): filed a rollback option for runtime v3.12.0 -> v3.11.8 if pattern repeats. Also gathering heap snapshots and redis kvcache keys for investigation.
incident-bot: PD12345 status: acknowledged by sam at 09:12 UTC.
sam (oncall): quick customer-impact summary for handoff: 09:09-09:22 UTC 3 hosted customers saw ~2-3x error spike, about 1500 requests failed total, routing fallback prevented larger outage for tiered customers. Root cause suspected kvcache eviction regression in runtime v3.12.0 (affects infer-gpu-* pools).
anya (oncall-next): taking handoff 09:35 UTC. My immediate plan: monitor for repeat OOMs for 30m, keep fallback routing in place, coordinate with infra to collect redis kvcache dump and runtime core dumps. If we see another PD, escalate to SEV1 and trigger rollback.
sam (oncall): handoff notes added to SRE-4392, including commands used, logs, and links to dashboards: https://grafana.example/d/abc/gpu-metrics?orgId=1
sam (oncall): leaving: make sure to capture `dmesg` from g-7-15 and redis `KVS:info` before restarting more nodes.
anya (oncall-next): ack — will keep watch and post updates.
incident-bot: auto-check at 09:30:00 UTC shows metric nv_gpu_mem_used_pct for infer-gpu-7 back below threshold (avg 42%), PD12345 auto-resolve timer started.
pagerduty-bot: PD12345 status: resolved by system at 09:40 UTC (auto-resolve).
leo (infra): next actions assigned: (1) replicate locally with load tester to repro kvcache growth (owner: leo), (2) prepare rollback play (owner: infra), (3) postmortem draft (owner: sam). ETA for postmortem draft 48h.
nina (sre): I notified account managers for cust-a/b/c, they have been sent an incident summary and are copy-looped.
sam (oncall): closing notes: mitigation worked but root cause likely codepath regression — require rollback or fix. handing off to anya for monitoring and post-incident follow-up. :white_check_mark:
anya (oncall-next): thanks — will ping if anything flares. :eyes:
